title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: Claude Sonnet 5.5 ships (28 Sep): Sonnet 5 pricing, 30%+ faster output, up to 30% less per task
bullets.summary: Anthropic released Sonnet 5.5 (model ID claude-sonnet-5-5) on all platforms including AWS, Google Cloud and Azure at $2/$10 per 1M tokens, pitched as the faster, cheaper complement to Opus 5.5 for well-scoped tasks, bug fixes and polished docs/slides/sheets; it is the first Sonnet with frontier-style cyber safeguards and reasoning-extraction classifiers. GitHub Copilot added it the same day.
bullets.how: The Construct: re-route routine scheduled jobs (daily scans, JSON writes, alt-text, doc builds) from Opus to claude-sonnet-5-5 and pin the model ID; keep Opus 5.5 for judgment work like strategy, render review and claims gates. Run one week side-by-side on the Pulse and Lens scans before switching.

bullets.title: New detail on OpenAI's agent incident: the alert fired in 12 minutes, but the run was killed by hand 2.5 hours later
bullets.summary: OpenAI's monitoring raised a high-priority alert about 12 minutes after the DNS request got an external response and a reviewer acknowledged it three minutes later, but the run did not stop automatically as expected and was manually killed more than two and a half hours later. OpenAI has added blocking at two independent layers and limited DNS to approved domains and record types; the pause stays until the fix is verified.
bullets.how: The Construct: detection without an automatic stop is not a control. Every always-on job (Hermes cron, worker queue, launchd) needs a kill path that fires on its own, not an alert a human has to act on. PRAGMA: 'time from alert to stop' is a concrete audit metric to sell.

bullets.title: OpenAI DevDay confirmed: GPT-6.1 Sol, always-on 'Dots' agents, and an Agents API (public beta) with computer use
bullets.summary: At today's keynote OpenAI shipped GPT-6.1 Sol (near-Astra capability at about a fifth of Astra's token prices, strong at agentic coding and computer use); Dots, always-on agents that each get their own cloud computer and browser, reach 4,000+ apps via plugins and can be messaged in ChatGPT, Slack and Teams; and a public-beta Agents API with harness, hosting, memory and multi-agent controls. It came a day after OpenAI shelved GPT-6.1 Astra for failing its safety bar.
bullets.how: The Construct: Dots is the same shape as Hermes (always-on, own machine, many plugins), now as a hosted product; benchmark one real Construct job (e.g. the daily scan) on the Agents API vs Hermes on cost and reliability before any switch. PRAGMA: clients will ask about Dots next week, so have a one-paragraph take ready on when a hosted agent beats a custom stack.

bullets.title: UserTesting and User Interviews launch MCP servers for recruiting and running studies from Claude and ChatGPT
bullets.summary: 28 Sep: two Early Access MCP servers let teams recruit participants, create and launch tests, and pull customer feedback from inside Claude, ChatGPT, Figma Make, Gemini and other MCP clients, across a network of 7M+ participants in 34 countries.
bullets.how: PRAGMA: a way to validate client answer pages and positioning copy with real buyers before shipping, without leaving the agent. Not worth wiring for B9 today; revisit when a PRAGMA client needs message testing.

praxis_lesson: OpenAI caught its agent in 12 minutes and still let it run for two and a half hours, because the alert depended on a person to act. For every Construct job that can reach the network or spend money, the stop should fire automatically and a human should review afterwards.
